title: Product Color Variations in One Matching Set | AIVideosUGC
description: Show product color variations in matching square photos, one for each shade you sell. Upload a photo of every colorway and build your swatch set today.
h1: Product Color Variations Shot in the Same Light and Setting
lead: Product color variations work best when only the color changes. Every colorway gets its own square photo with the same table, light, and angle, so shoppers can compare shades without a change of backdrop getting in the way.
intro: The example lines up four low-top canvas sneakers in cream, navy, black, and olive on a linen runner. The light, the wooden table, and the low angle stay the same, so the only thing that changes is the color.

That consistency matters when a buyer taps between swatches on a Shopify product page or an Amazon variation. If each shade was shot on a different day in a different room, the colors are hard to compare. Make one photo per color with the same description, and the photos read as one set.
tip: Upload a photo of the actual product in each color rather than one pair to be recolored, because real dyes and fabric textures differ more than you'd expect.

steps.d: Take one photo per color from the same angle and in the same daylight, so the starting points already match.

steps.t: Write one description and keep it
steps.d: Describe the setting once, for example "linen runner on a light oak table," and paste the same words for each color.

steps.t: Attach each photo to its swatch
steps.d: Download each result and assign it to the matching variant in Shopify or Amazon, so the right image shows when a shopper picks a color.

ideas.d: When you add a color for spring or fall, make its photo in the same setting so it slots into the set you already have.
Any item sold in several colors, from T-shirts to canvas bags, can follow the same one-setting approach.
Post the shades as a swipeable carousel, one color per slide, to introduce a full range.

faq.q: Can I make every color from a single photo?
faq.a: Upload each colorway separately. Recoloring one photo can miss how a fabric or dye really looks, and buyers expect the shade they see to be the shade they receive.

faq.q: How many colors can I make?
faq.a: As many as you sell. Each color is a separate run with its own credit cost shown before it starts, so a sneaker in six shades means six runs.

faq.q: How do I stop the background from changing between colors?
faq.a: Keep your description word for word the same and upload photos taken from the same angle. If one result drifts, run that color again.

faq.q: Can I keep the same framing across product colors?
faq.a: Use the same camera and background wording for each run, then compare the outputs side by side. Each color is a separate job, so review the product identity before publishing.

overview.h2: Make Every Swatch Feel Like Part of One Product
overview.p: When a shopper taps from black to cream, the product should stay in the same place and the setting should stay quiet. A coordinated colorway set keeps the comparison on the shade instead of making the shopper compare different rooms, crops, or camera angles.

overview.h2: Use the Real Item for Every Variant
overview.p: Different dyes, materials, and finishes react differently to light. Supply a source photo for each shade you sell, then reuse the scene description so the setting remains stable while the product color changes.

items.d: Photograph the actual black, cream, olive, or seasonal item rather than asking one shade to stand in for the rest.
Use the same distance, tilt, crop, and product orientation for every source image.
Choose neutral daylight and avoid a colored wall or strong reflection that shifts how the shade reads.
Use the catalog color name in your notes so a downloaded file cannot be attached to the wrong swatch.

results.h2: A Variant Set Built for Comparison

items.d: Keep the table, backdrop, and shadow language aligned across the collection.
Let shoppers compare shape, stitching, and proportions without a new angle in every file.
Give each Shopify or Amazon variant its own supporting image.
Use the result to support the swatch, then verify the physical color before treating it as a catalog reference.

scene_recipes.h2: Colorway Sets for More Than Sneakers

items.d: Cream, navy, black, and olive pairs on a linen runner with the same low side angle.
Four matte bottles aligned on a pale kitchen counter with identical caps facing forward.
Natural, rust, and charcoal totes hanging from the same wooden peg in soft window light.
Small tubes standing upright on a stone tray, with each cap facing the same direction.

after_download.h2: Audit the Set Before Linking Variants

items.d: Check hue, finish, stitching, and hardware against each item in your inventory.
Use a simple filename such as product-color so the correct image follows the correct swatch.
Type your approved color name, price, and availability in the store system rather than inside the generated image.

good: Apparel, footwear, bags, bottles, and accessories sold in clear colorways
Products with similar shape across variants
Shopify or Amazon catalogs using swatches
Social carousels introducing a new seasonal shade
not_ideal: Products whose color depends on an exact calibrated print proof
Variants with different shapes or packaging in every color
Highly reflective finishes that change dramatically with the light
